extracted.intended_audience: political thinkers, legislators, and engaged citizens evaluating constitutional design (late-18th-century France/British comparative audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for assessing a constitution's structure and practical fitness — especially representation (bases: territory, population, contribution), electoral qualifications, unity/cohesion, and accommodation to human nature and local circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of ability in framers
rubrics_metrics.description: Men who undertake considerable things, even in a regular way, ought to give us ground to presume ability. But the physician of the state who... undertakes to regenerate constitutions ought to show uncommon powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislators or framers of a constitution must demonstrate practical competence and uncommon powers; grand constitutional projects require demonstrable ability beyond mere theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess spirit, tendency, fitness, and internal consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider its spirit, its tendency, and its fitness for framing a popular commonwealth... At the same time I mean to consider its consistency with itself and its own principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each part (legislature, executive, judicature, army, finance) for whether it serves the declared ends and whether the parts cohere with the constitution's stated principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge by effects and practical outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Old establishments are tried by their effects. If the people are happy, united, wealthy, and powerful, we presume the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give weight to empirical results (social welfare, unity, prosperity, stability) rather than purely theoretical elegance when judging a constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid purely theoretic or abstract construction
rubrics_metrics.description: In a new and merely theoretic system, it is expected that every contrivance shall appear, on the face of it, to answer its ends... The French builders... forming everything into an exact level...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional design must account for practical realities and local habits rather than imposing abstract geometric/arithmetic plans disconnected from human circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect local conditions over arbitrary geometrical divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: They divide the area of their country into eighty-three pieces, regularly square... it is impossible that innumerable local inconveniences... must not arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Territorial subdivisions should reflect existing local conditions, usages, and institutions; avoid rigid square-measure divisions that ignore geography, economy, and habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify and reconcile bases of representation (territory/population/contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: They propose to rest the whole local and general legislature on three bases... territory, population, and contribution... they allotted one of those parts to the square measurement, without a single fact or calculation to ascertain whether this territorial proportion... ought upon any principle really to be a third.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple bases are used, their relative weights must be justified with facts and coherent reasoning; arbitrary allocations (e.g., one-third to territory) are invalid without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral qualifications must align with proclaimed equality
rubrics_metrics.description: What! a qualification on the indefeasible rights of men? Yes; but it shall be a very small qualification... it excludes from a vote the man of all others whose natural equality stands the most in need of protection...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifications (property, tax payments) that contradict the stated principle of natural equality are illegitimate; avoid small property thresholds that disenfranchise the poorest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve accountable connection between representatives and constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: There is little, or rather no, connection between the last representative and the first constituent. The member who goes to the National Assembly is not chosen by the people, nor accountable to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design representation and electoral steps to ensure meaningful accountability and communication between elector and representative; minimize unnecessary intermediary layers that sever this link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by contribution should consider individuals, not only districts
rubrics_metrics.description: The additional share in the third portion of representation... is made to regard the district only, and not the individuals in it who pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If wealth/contribution informs representation, measure contribution at the appropriate level (individual or clearly justified aggregate) so the rich are not unfairly advantaged or misrepresented by district aggregates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer indirect contribution metrics to direct contribution for equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The indirect contribution, that which arises from duties on consumption, is in truth a better standard and follows and discovers wealth more naturally than this of direct contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using fiscal measures to gauge wealth or contribution, indirect measures (consumption duties) may better reflect real wealth distribution than direct assessment methods that misattribute contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent constitution's dependence on variable taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: Their taxation does not so much depend on their constitution as their constitution on their taxation. This must introduce great confusion...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not design electoral qualifications or constitutional structures that vary with tax regimes; a constitution should be stable and not contingent on fluctuating fiscal systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study human nature and classify citizens by real differences
rubrics_metrics.description: They had to do with men, and they were obliged to study human nature... diversities... birth, education, professions, the periods of their lives, their residence in towns or in the country...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective constitutions account for social, economic, and professional differences, creating arrangements or classes appropriate to distinct civic roles rather than assuming homogeneous citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain social distinctions and indirect restraints to prevent despotism
rubrics_metrics.description: They have leveled and crushed together all the orders... For want of something of this kind, if the present project of a republic should fail, all securities to a moderated freedom fail along with it...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid wholesale leveling that removes traditional mediating institutions; certain social distinctions and intermediary bodies can act as safeguards against absolute power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure central, standing government to secure unity
rubrics_metrics.description: This standing, unalterable, fundamental government would make, and it is the only thing which could make, that territory truly and properly a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a durable central authority (a trustee for the whole) to bind subdivisions together, ensuring that deputies represent the nation as a whole and not only parochial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fragmenting the nation into independent republics
rubrics_metrics.description: This scheme... has a direct and immediate tendency to sever France into a variety of republics, and to render them totally independent of each other without any direct constitutional means of coherence...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design constitutional mechanisms for coherence, subordination, and interdependence to prevent disunion and rivalry among subdivisions that can destabilize the whole state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint officials familiar with their districts
rubrics_metrics.description: Magistrates and collectors of revenue are now no longer acquainted with their districts, bishops with their dioceses, or curates with their parishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative and local officials should have local knowledge and connection to their jurisdictions to preserve good governance and civil discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware incentives that multiply offices and encourage demagoguery
rubrics_metrics.description: The increase of representation within his province sets up nine persons more... An interest is by this means held out to multitudes of the inferior sort, in obtaining a salary... besides the pleasure of a residence in Paris and their share in the government of the kingdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid institutional designs that create many remunerated offices or ambitions that encourage demagogues to flatter and exploit the poor; excessive multiplication of posts can increase faction and instability.
